implementation_notes: Rust's enum is a sum type with a compiler-generated tag: each variant may carry a different payload (unit, tuple or named fields) and match enforces exhaustive coverage while binding payloads by destructuring, so a new variant breaks compilation at every eliminator. Products are structs or tuples, Box supplies indirection for recursive variants, and Option/Result are ordinary prelude enums rather than special syntax. Deriving Debug, Clone and PartialEq is routine because the enum is a normal value type; if let and let else handle the single-variant case without giving up the type.
pitfalls: match on an owned enum moves it unless the payloads are Copy; matching a borrowed value (or the match ergonomics of a reference) is the usual borrow-checker stumbling block.
A recursive variant must be boxed (or otherwise indirect) or the type has infinite size; enum recursion also means Drop runs on the whole spine.
#[non_exhaustive] on a public enum forces downstream matches to keep a wildcard arm, so the compiler can no longer catch a missing variant in other crates.
Large payloads are stored inline in the enum, so the whole value is as big as the largest variant; box big variants to keep the common case cheap.
